findings.title: Removed bullet badge margin-top rule without replacement
findings.body: The `.extra-info-wrapper .badge-wrapper.bullet { margin-top: 5px; }` rule is deleted, so bullet badges inside the extra-info wrapper lose their 5px top offset. Nothing in the diff compensates for this, so the bullet alignment in the topic title area will shift. The removal is not explained by the stated flexbox change.

findings.title: order(2) and line-height change have no effect unless the parent is a flex container
findings.body: `@include order(2)` only works on flex or box children. The diff does not make the parent of `.extra-info-wrapper` a flex container, so the ordering is a no-op there. The added `line-height: 1.5` also changes text layout for all content in this wrapper, which the PR does not mention.

findings.title: Header .title float rule removed, layout depends on flex without verification
findings.body: The `.title { float: left; }` rule is removed and `.contents` becomes a flex container, while `.panel` drops `float: right` for `margin-left: auto`. Any element still relying on the removed float or on normal block flow inside `.d-header .contents` will reflow differently. The change is a wholesale layout rewrite with no evidence it was checked across header states (logged in, anon, narrow widths).

findings.title: small-action-desc padding and spacing removed, changes post layout
findings.body: The padding `0.5em 0 0.5em 4em` and `margin-top: 5px` are replaced by `padding: 0 1.5%`, and the `p` margin and `> p` padding-top are also removed. The left indent of the small-action text drops from 4em to about 1.5%, and vertical spacing shrinks. These are visual regressions in small-action rows (closed, pinned, etc.), not performance changes.

findings.title: Floats inside a new flex container are ignored
findings.body: `.small-action` becomes a flex container, but its children still use `float: left` (`.topic-avatar`, `.avatar`) and `button { float: right }`. Floats are ignored on flex items, so the float-based layout the rules were written for no longer applies. The author should confirm the intended positioning.

findings.title: align-items mixin emits invalid -ms-align-items property
findings.body: The mixin outputs `-ms-align-items`, which is not a real property in any vendor prefix set. Browsers ignore it, and it adds dead output. Its `-ms-flex-align` line is the correct prefixed form.

findings.title: New flexbox mixins may duplicate existing definitions
findings.body: `flexbox`, `inline-flex`, `align-items` and `order` are appended here, but the same mixin names may already exist elsewhere in the theme. Duplicate `@mixin` definitions silently override each other depending on import order, which can change output. Confirm no other definitions exist.

findings.title: Inline-flex mixin adds prefixed display values that differ from the original rule
findings.body: The original `display: inline-flex; align-items: baseline;` is replaced by mixins that also emit `-webkit-inline-box` and `-moz-inline-box` before the standard value. Vendor-specific box display values are not equivalent to flex and can conflict in older engines. The PR does not justify this change.

findings.title: PR title and description do not match the change
findings.body: The title says the change optimizes header layout performance, but the diff is purely layout restyling with visual side effects (spacing, float removal, margin removal). The description is only 'Test 5', so reviewers have no rationale, no before/after measurements, and no testing notes.
